content:
incident-bot: P1 alert: sudden regression on kv-cache path in prod-east (us-east-1). Symptoms: large latency tail and increased gen errors. link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/incidents/67890
jia: ack. paging @lee @alex @nina. oncall=jia. quick summary pls — any recent config pushes?
lee: seeing spike starting ~2026-03-15T18:03Z. Errors peaking ~7% on chat/generate; token latency p99 up x6. Recent rollout note: continuous-batching v2.1 pushed 18:00 with new reuse heuristics.
ops-bot: Deploy event: config continuous-batching=v2.1 by platform-ci at 2026-03-15T18:00:12 (change-id=cb-20260315-18).
alex: tailing runtime logs now. sample errors:
```
[2026-03-15T18:04:02Z] ERROR runtime.kvcache tenant=shopwise req=tx-111 key=session:49 cache_seq=90012 request_seq=1003 mismatch
[2026-03-15T18:04:02Z] WARN runtime: possible cross-req cache-hit tenant=shopwise req=tx-112 reused_key=session:49
[2026-03-15T18:04:03Z] ERROR runtime: output_corruption tenant=shopwise req=tx-113 cause=kv_value_stale
```
nina: confirmed impact: multi-tenant streaming sessions with long context are most affected. Estimated affected traffic ~120k rps, error window ~6 minutes. Top customers: shopwise (~15% of errors), datafold (~10%).
jia: mitigation plan proposal: 1) quick toggle to set kv_reuse=false across us-east; 2) rollback continuous-batching to v2.0 if toggle insufficient; 3) add temporary per-request seq verification to reject reuse. Agree?
lee: I'll flip kv_reuse flag now. Command:
```
redis-cli -h config-store set runtime:flags:kv_reuse false
```
ops-bot: Flag applied to config-store cluster-2. Propagating to runtimes (rolling). 5/10 nodes acknowledged so far.
alex: adding hotfix: insert seq-guard in lookup path to return miss on seq mismatch. Pushing as config patch to runtime via configmap. Patch applied to 4/10 nodes (hotpatch job).
runtime-bot: Hotpatch job status: 4 succeeded, 6 pending. Noted two nodes failed to restart due to OOM during patch; autoscaler started replacements.
lee: logs after kv_reuse=false and seq-guard on partial fleet show error-rate dropping from ~7% to ~1.2% in patched subset. Still seeing intermittent stale-value errors where old values are served if cache_addr collision occurs.
jia: customer-facing: CSMs notified for shopwise and datafold. CSM note: transient generation errors affecting some streaming sessions; we rolled back config and disabled reuse; follow-up with root cause and remediation.
alex: rollback attempt for continuous-batching v2.1 -> v2.0 initiated (change-id=cb-rollback-67890). Rolling replace of config on 10 pods, ETA ~2m.
nina: reproducer: running high-concurrency stream replay against staging with v2.1 + kv_reuse=true produces cross-request hits when batching window >=300ms and sequence wrapping occurs on large contexts. Minimal repro steps posted to gist: https://gist.internal/rep/kv-repro
lee: immediate runbook summary for on-call: - toggle off kv_reuse fast; - if errors persist, rollback continuous-batching; - scale up workers if OOMs during patch; - collect full per-req trace (req_id, cache_seq, request_seq, tenant).
ops-bot: Rollback complete: continuous-batching v2.1 -> v2.0 applied to all 10 pods.
jia: status check: error-rate now ~0.6%, latency near-normal. Downgrading severity to P2 and switching to monitoring/watch. Leaving hotpatch and logs collection in-progress.
alex: follow-ups I'm owning: (1) add strict per-request namespace to cache keys to avoid collisions (owner=alex), (2) implement seq-check as fail-open hit->miss (owner=alex), (3) add CI replay harness for multi-tenant long-context streaming (owner=nina).
nina: also adding canary gating for any future continuous-batching changes that touch reuse heuristics. Canary must run long-context multi-tenant scenario for 30m before rollout.
jia: handoff: alex taking overnight watch. I'll create incident doc and ping PMs + CSMs. Postmortem due EOD +72h.
runtime-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://incidents/1803457001/artifacts/logs.tar.gz, s3://incidents/1803457001/trace-replay.jsonl
lee: note for postmortem: we should consider adding sequence-id entropy in key namespace when shard collisions are possible (e.g., high-concurrency reuse).
alex: one observation: continuous-batching v2.1 changed the reuse cutoff from per-request to per-session heuristic; combined with a small bug in seq offset calculation it allowed values written for earlier request batches to be served to later requests. Fix plan: revert heuristic change, add unit tests, add seq-offset assertion.
jia: thanks team. Monitor for 2h then close if stable. If anything spikes, re-page using same chain. :thumbsup:
